```{r}
source("_common.R")
families <- stv$stv_families()
defaults <- stv$stv_default_settings()
glossary <- stv$stv_glossary()
examples <- stv$stv_examples()
```

# About this guide

stabilitest.viz is a web application for the stabilitest R package. stabilitest asks
how easily a statistical conclusion could be overturned; the app lets you ask that
question of your own data without writing code, then read, compare and export the
answer.

This guide is for anyone who runs analyses in the app: statisticians, clinical
reviewers and students. It walks through the five steps of an analysis, explains every
part of a result, and covers comparison, export and the two modes of the app. The
*Technical documentation* describes how the app is built and deployed.

Two rules hold throughout the app, and they shape what you see:

- **Every number comes from stabilitest.** The app computes no statistics of its own.
  It prepares your data, calls stabilitest, and displays what stabilitest returns.
- **A label appears only when stabilitest gives one.** A categorical label such as
  *Fragile* needs a validated calibration. Where none exists, the app shows the score
  as a number and says so; it never colours a score red or green on its own.

# Getting started

## Starting the app

In R, install the package once and start the app:

```r
pak::pak("ma-brain/stabilitest.viz")
stabilitest.viz::run_app()
```

The app opens in your browser. Your organisation may instead run it on a server or
from the Docker image, in which case you only need the address.

## Profiles

The app runs under one of three profiles, chosen by whoever starts it. The profile sets
limits and which features are available.

```{r}
md_table(profiles_table())
```

## The screen

The bar at the top has four pages: **Analyse**, where analyses are run; **Compare**,
which lines up analyses from this session; **Learn**, which explains the three stress
tests; and **About**, with versions, the calibration registry and the citation. On the
right are the **Guided / Expert** switch (not in the public profile) and the light/dark
switch.

On the Analyse page, the steps of an analysis are in the panel on the left, and the
data and results on the right. The left panel can be collapsed with the arrow at its top.

# An analysis in five steps

The steps are numbered 1 to 5. A tick appears next to each step that is complete.

## 1. Data

Choose a bundled example or, unless the profile turns uploads off, upload a file.

```{r}
screenshot("step-data", "The Data step.", "40%")
```

**Files.** CSV, TSV and text files, Excel workbooks (`.xlsx`, `.xls`, with a choice of
sheet), SAS transport files (`.xpt`) and SAS data sets (`.sas7bdat`) are read. SAS
variable labels are kept and shown as tooltips on column names.

**Bundled examples.**

```{r}
md_table(data.frame(Example = examples$label, Source = examples$group))
```

**Preview.** Once data are loaded, the right side shows the number of rows, columns,
missing cells and subjects, the type of each column, the first rows, and a suggested
mapping of columns to roles.

```{r}
screenshot("data-preview", "Data preview with the suggested mapping.")
```

**ADaM data.** When the data look like a CDISC ADaM data set (ADSL, a BDS data set
such as ADEFF or ADLB, or ADTTE), the app recognises it from the column names, offers
filters for the parameter (`PARAMCD`), visit (`AVISIT`) and population flags
(`SAFFL`, `ITTFL`, `EFFFL`), and suggests the usual mapping: `AVAL` or `CHG` as
outcome, `TRT01P` or `TRTP` as group, `BASE` as covariate, and `AVAL` with `CNSR`
(inverted to an event) for time-to-event data.

**One row per subject.** stabilitest treats each row as one independent observation.
If a subject appears on several rows, for example several visits, the app says so and
does not run until filters leave one row per subject. Paired data in long layout are
the exception.

## 2. Question

Choose the family of analysis by the question you want to ask, then the test within it.

```{r}
screenshot("step-question", "The Question step.", "40%")
```

```{r}
tests <- vapply(families$id, \(f) {
  t <- names(stv$stv_tests(f))
  if (length(t)) paste(t, collapse = ", ") else "One model"
}, character(1))
md_table(data.frame(Family = families$label, Question = families$question, Tests = tests))
```

The app suggests a family from the data: a 0/1 outcome points to proportions, two
measurement columns to a paired test.

## 3. Map

Tell the app which column plays which role. Only columns that fit a role are offered,
and the same column cannot take two roles.

```{r}
screenshot("step-map", "The Map step for two groups.", "40%")
```

| Family | Roles |
|---|---|
| Two groups (continuous) | Outcome and group, then which level is group 1 and group 2. Paired tests take a first and second measurement instead. |
| Two proportions | A 0/1 response and a group. |
| Equivalence or non-inferiority | Outcome, group and levels, the margin, whether higher values are better and, for means, whether the measurements are paired. |
| Linear model | Outcome, predictors (treatment and covariates), reference levels, and the term to test. |
| Generalised linear model | Outcome (0/1 for binomial, counts for Poisson), predictors, an optional offset such as exposure time for Poisson, and the term. |
| Cox model | Time, event (with an option for data coded the other way, such as `CNSR`), predictors and the term. |

Effects are group 1 minus group 2. If something does not fit, for example an outcome
with only two values in a t-test, the step says why and suggests the fitting family.

## 4. Settings

```{r}
screenshot("step-settings", "Settings in Guided mode.", "40%")
```

```{r}
md_table(data.frame(
  Setting = c(
    "Significance level (alpha)", "Bootstrap resamples", "Score weights", "Maximum removal",
    "Influence threshold", "Seed", "Write an interpretation"
  ),
  Default = c(
    format(defaults$alpha), format(defaults$n_boot),
    paste(paste0(names(defaults$weights), " ", round(100 * defaults$weights), "%"), collapse = ", "),
    paste0(round(100 * defaults$max_removal_pct), "% of observations"),
    paste("change in p of", format(defaults$influential_threshold)), format(defaults$seed),
    if (isTRUE(defaults$interpret)) "On" else "Off"
  ),
  `What it does` = c(
    "The level at which the original analysis is called significant.",
    "How many resamples the bootstrap draws. More is steadier and slower.",
    "How the three components are weighted in the composite score; they add to 100%.",
    "The most observations the worst-case search may remove.",
    "How much a leave-one-out p-value must move for an observation to be flagged (two-group tests).",
    "Makes resampling repeatable: the same seed gives the same result.",
    "Asks stabilitest to write a text interpretation (two-group tests)."
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

Guided mode shows the significance level and resamples; the other settings are in
Expert mode. The profile may cap the number of resamples, and the default is lowered to
that cap.

**Validated Fisher settings.** For the Fisher exact test, a button applies the settings
of the one validated calibration profile. With these settings, and data that
stabilitest finds eligible, stabilitest returns a categorical label. The button sets the
settings only: whether a label is returned is stabilitest's decision.

## 5. Run

Press **Run analysis**. The analysis runs in the background, so the app stays usable,
and a run can be cancelled. For long runs the step shows an estimate of the time. If the
setup has a problem, Run lists it instead of running.

# Reading a result

A result appears below the data, in three parts: the calibration banner, the score
row, and, in Guided mode, a plain-language panel.

```{r}
screenshot("results-score", "The banner and score row of a result without a label.")
```

## The calibration banner

The banner says whether stabilitest returned a categorical label.

- **No categorical label** (grey). The method or setting has no validated cutoff. The
  score and its parts are numbers to read, compare and discuss; a low or high score
  is not called fragile or robust. A blank label is deliberate: it does not mean the
  analysis failed.
- **A label** (coloured). stabilitest returned a label under a validated calibration,
  for example *Fragile* for a significant Fisher exact test under the validated
  settings. Only then does the app use colour for the verdict.

```{r}
screenshot("results-label", "A result with a label returned by stabilitest.")
```

## The score row

```{r}
md_table(data.frame(
  Box = c("Composite score", "Jackknife stability", "Removal fragility", "Bootstrap same-decision rate",
    "Original p-value"),
  Meaning = unlist(glossary[c("composite", "jackknife", "fragility", "bootstrap", "p_value")])
))
```

Each component box shows its weight in the score. The line under the row writes out
the score from the weights and components stabilitest returned, so you can see how it
was formed. Every box has an info button with its definition.

The removal fragility box also says after how many observations the decision changed,
for example *Decision flips after removing 6 obs (10.9%)*. When the decision did not
change within the maximum removal, it says so.

## What does this mean?

In Guided mode, a panel restates the result in plain sentences: the original decision,
how many removals change it, how often leaving out one observation or resampling keeps
it, and what can be said about the score. Each sentence repeats a number stabilitest
returned. Without a label, the panel says that the score is not called fragile or
robust.

```{r}
screenshot("results-meaning", "The plain-language panel in Guided mode.")
```

# Exploring a result

Below the score, tabs show each part of the result in detail. In Expert mode the tabs
open on Code.

## Removal path

The p-value after removing one, two, three and more observations, each time the one
that moves the p-value furthest toward the other decision. The dashed horizontal line is
alpha; a ring marks the step at which the decision changes. For two-group tests a
second, dashed path removes the most extreme values instead, for comparison; it is not
part of the score. Hover over a point to see which observation was removed.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-removal-path", "The Removal path tab.")
```

## Influence

Each point is the p-value with one observation left out. The solid line is the original
p-value, the dashed line alpha. Observations stabilitest flags as influential are
marked. Click a point, or drag over several, to list their rows from the data below the
plot. A selection here also ticks those observations in the Removed observations tab.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-influence", "The Influence tab.")
```

## Bootstrap

The distribution of p-values across the bootstrap resamples, split into resamples that
reach the same decision and those that do not. The share reaching the same decision is
the bootstrap same-decision rate. It describes this data set; it is not the probability
that a new study would repeat the result.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-bootstrap", "The Bootstrap tab.")
```

## Removed observations

The observations the worst-case path removed, in order, with the p-value after each
removal, whether the decision had changed, and the full row from the data. The step at
which the decision changes is highlighted. Tick rows to ring them in the Influence plot.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-removed-observations", "The Removed observations tab.")
```

## Interpretation

Text written by stabilitest for two-group tests when *Write an interpretation* is on:
an overall statement, one paragraph per stress test, and a recommendation.

## Code

R code that reproduces the result outside the app: reading the data, the filters, the
preparation and the stabilitest call, with the seed. A **Copy** button copies it.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-code", "The Code tab.")
```

# Comparing analyses

Every analysis run in a session is kept. On the **Compare** page, tick the analyses to
compare; the latest four are ticked to start. They appear side by side with the same
rows as the report summary, and their worst-case removal paths are drawn on one plot. If
the analyses were run on different data or different filters, a note says so, because
their numbers are then not directly comparable. Analyses can be removed one by one or
all at once. Nothing is kept after the session ends.

```{r}
screenshot("compare", "Three tests of the same data on the Compare page.")
```

# Exporting

The **Export** tab of a result offers:

| Export | Formats | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Report | HTML, Word, PDF | The summary and calibration statement, the three plots, the removed and influential observations, the interpretation, the code and software versions. |
| Plots | PNG, SVG | The removal path, influence or bootstrap plot, on a light background. |
| Tables | XLSX (all), CSV (one) | The summary, metrics, removal paths, jackknife and bootstrap results, and the removed observations with their data rows. |
| R script | `.R` | The code from the Code tab. |
| Result | `.rds` | The object stabilitest returned, for further work in R. |

The report needs Quarto on the machine running the app. If it is missing, the tab says
so and the other exports still work.

```{r}
screenshot("tab-export", "The Export tab.")
```

# Guided and Expert modes

| | Guided | Expert |
|---|---|---|
| Settings | Significance level and resamples | All settings |
| Data filters | ADaM filters | ADaM filters and a free row filter |
| Results | "What does this mean?" panel; tabs open on Removal path | No panel; tabs open on Code |

Switch with the control at the top right. The public profile is always Guided.

```{r}
screenshot("step-settings-expert", "Settings in Expert mode.", "30%")
```

# Questions and answers

**Why does my result have no label?** stabilitest has a validated calibration for one
setting today (the Fisher exact test, significant, under the validated settings). For
every other method the score is reported as a number. This is deliberate.

**Is a score of 30 fragile?** Without a label, the app and stabilitest do not say. Read
the components: after how many removals the decision changes, and how often
resampling keeps it. Comparing analyses of the same data on the Compare page can help.

**Why will the analysis not run?** The Run step lists the reason, for example more than
one row per subject, a column used in two roles, or more resamples than the profile
allows.

**Why do two runs give slightly different bootstrap numbers?** They used different
seeds. With the same seed and settings, results are identical.

**Does the bootstrap same-decision rate tell me whether the trial will replicate?** No.
It describes how stable the decision is in resamples of this data set.

**Where are my analyses stored?** Only in your browser session, until it closes.

# Glossary

```{r}
md_table(data.frame(
  Term = c("Composite score", "Jackknife stability", "Removal fragility", "Bootstrap same-decision rate",
    "Original p-value", "Calibration", "Fail-closed"),
  Definition = c(
    unlist(glossary[c("composite", "jackknife", "fragility", "bootstrap", "p_value")]),
    "Evidence, from simulation studies, that a score cutoff separates fragile from robust results for a method and setting.",
    "When no validated calibration applies, no label is shown and the score stays a number."
  )
))
```
